record.what_it_does: Shared-inbox customer support platform with email, chat, Docs knowledge base and reports.
record.auth_notes: The Inbox (Mailbox) API 2.0 supports only OAuth2. The Authorization Code flow is for integrations used by other Help Scout users. The Client Credentials flow, which uses your app ID and secret, is for internal integrations. Tokens are Bearer tokens. A Client Credentials token is valid for 2 days, and expiry is signalled by HTTP 401. Authorization Code tokens come with refresh tokens. The OAuth app is created under Your Profile > My apps, and a redirect URL is required for the Authorization Code flow. The Mailbox API has no personal access token. The separate Docs API uses an API key, passed as the username in HTTP Basic auth with a dummy password 'X'. A multi-user toolkit would use the Authorization Code flow for the Mailbox API, plus an optional per-user Docs API key.
record.access_notes: The pricing page lists a Free plan (5 users, 1 Inbox, 1 Docs site), but its 'API access' row shows no value for Free. API access appears on the paid plans with plan-based rate limits: 200, 400 and 800 calls per minute, most likely for Standard, Plus and Pro. Help Scout's MCP article confirms that Standard, Plus and Pro are the plans that include API access. Standard and Plus offer a self-serve 15-day trial with no credit card that includes 'all of the plan's features', so a developer can probably test the API during a trial. That is inferred and not stated explicitly. The Pro trial goes through sales. Creating an OAuth app is self-serve (Owner or Admin role, under My apps). The developer docs I checked describe no review or approval step for Authorization Code apps.
record.api_breadth_notes: The base URL is https://api.helpscout.net/v2. The Inbox API 2.0 reference has 13 resource groups with about 149 operations: Conversations 29, Customers 33, Inboxes 11, Organizations 14, Properties 4, Ratings 1, Reports 32, System-users 2, Tags 2, Teams 3, Users 10, Webhooks 5 and Workflows 3. The Docs API adds Articles, Assets, Categories, Collections, Redirects and Sites. All users on an account share one rate limit, which depends on the plan. Writes count as 2 requests.
record.mcp_notes: Help Scout's official connector is at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp. Each user signs in with OAuth on Help Scout's own login page, and the connector registers itself, so a client ID and secret are optional. A Docs API key is optional and only needed for Docs tools. The article names Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor as clients. The connector is available on Standard, Plus and Pro, and its report tools need Plus or Pro. A community server also exists (drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server), but I did not re-verify it.
record.blocker_notes: The Free plan has no API access, so end users need Standard, Plus or Pro. For development, a 15-day Standard or Plus trial with no credit card appears to work. The docs describe no separate sandbox and no app review for OAuth apps. Help Scout publishes no official OpenAPI spec; only third-party specs exist (for example, Jentic).
